title: Thirty-eight rhyolite domes
text: Volcanism began in the Coso Range about 6 million years ago. The region is best known for 38 high-silica rhyolite domes and lava flows that erupted in the Pleistocene, between about 1.1 million and 40,000 years ago, along with 14 basaltic centers. The domes form an elongate array atop a north-trending horst about 8 by 20 kilometers. The field's last listed eruption was about 39,000 years ago, though small episodes of ash emission and cone building may be Holocene in age.

s1.title: Geology and History of Coso Volcanic Field (October 30, 2023)
s1.quote: Volcanism began in the Coso Range approximately 6 million years ago ... The third period of activity occurred during the Pleistocene between about 1.1 and 0.04 million years ago. The region is most well known for the 38 high-silica rhyolite domes and lava flows that erupted during this time period. These well-known domes were accompanied by the eruption of 14 basaltic centers.
